featured_reviews.name: Arzan Dumasia
featured_reviews.review_text:
P.F. Chang’s at Lower Parel is one of those places you walk into with a certain set of expectations — especially for dinner. Big space, familiar menu, and that promise of bold Asian flavours. Our visit was mostly enjoyable, but a few things definitely held it back from being a great meal.

Let’s start with the biggest issue of the night — temperature. A surprising number of dishes arrived almost cold. Not “could be hotter” warm, but genuinely needing to be sent back. We had to request reheating more than once, which took away from the flow of the meal. For a restaurant of this scale and reputation, that was disappointing and honestly shouldn’t happen.

Drinks came first. The Samurai Fizz (2.5/5) was… fine. Refreshing, yes, but pretty forgettable. It didn’t really stand out in flavour. On the other hand, the Passionfruit Iced Tea (4.5/5) was excellent — well-balanced, refreshing, and easily the best drink we ordered.

Soups were a letdown. Both the Hot & Sour Soup (2/5) and Chang’s Noodle Soup (2/5) lacked depth and warmth — in flavour and temperature. They felt rushed and flat, which is a shame because these are usually comforting starters.

Things picked up once the appetisers started rolling in. The Shrimp Tempura Roll (4/5) was nicely done — crispy shrimp, clean flavours, and well-balanced textures. The Pan Fried Handmade Shrimp Dumplings (2/5), however, were underwhelming. Soft, yes, but bland and missing that punch you expect from dumplings.

Vegetarian dishes did surprisingly well. The Kung Pao Potatoes (4/5) were addictive — crispy, spicy, and full of flavour. Easily one of the better plates on the table.

Among the chicken dishes, both the Orange Chicken (4/5) and Dynamite Chicken (4/5) delivered what you expect — crispy, saucy, and comforting. No complaints there. But the real star of the night was the Ring of Fire Shrimp (5/5). Perfectly crispy, bold flavours, and just the right amount of heat. This dish alone made the wait and reheating worth it.

The Mongolian Tenderloin (3/5) was a mixed experience. The meat was beautifully tender, cooked just right, but the flavour was surprisingly bland. It needed more sauce or seasoning to really shine.

For sides, the Hong Kong Egg Fried Rice (4/5) was simple and satisfying, and the Chicken in Black Bean (4/5) was solid — comforting, flavourful, and reliable.

Desserts wrapped things up nicely. The Great Wall of Chocolate (4/5) was rich and indulgent without being too heavy, while the Banana Spring Roll (4/5) was crisp, warm, and a crowd-pleaser.

Where P.F. Chang’s really scored was service. The staff was extremely friendly, attentive, and handled the reheating requests politely and efficiently. They genuinely tried to make the experience better, which made a big difference. The atmosphere was pleasant — lively but not chaotic — making it a comfortable place for a dinner outing.

Overall, P.F. Chang’s Lower Parel had some strong dishes and excellent service, but the repeated issue of food being served cold brought the overall experience down. If they can fix that one major flaw, it would easily be a much better dining spot. Right now, it’s good — just not as great as it should be.

A Summer Feast at China Bistro, Kamala Mills

Dropped by China Bistro in Kamla Mills for lunch today, and I must say—it was an absolute treat. The moment you step in, you’re welcomed by a warm, elegant ambience that instantly sets the tone for a laid-back, indulgent meal. Tucked away in one of Mumbai’s most vibrant locations, this spot is as perfect for a casual lunch as it is for a proper culinary exploration.

They’re currently running a Summer Special Menu, and trust me, it’s something you don’t want to miss. From the moment I took a bite of the raw papaya salad, I knew I was in for something special. Crisp, tangy, just the right amount of spice—it was refreshing and full of flavour.
And then came the surprises—mango sushi (yes, you read that right!) which was so beautifully plated and unexpectedly delicious, and the tofu fries with mango salsa which I genuinely couldn’t get enough of. That salsa? Sweet, zesty, and addictive. Honestly, I’d go back just for that.
They also offer a buffet with a generous spread, so whether you're a vegetarian, non-veg lover, or vegan, there’s something for everyone. But here’s a little tip—do not skip the mango cheesecake. It’s creamy, smooth, and the perfect ending to this summer-inspired meal.
Everything I tried was incredibly fresh, well-balanced in flavour, and beautifully presented. The team here clearly knows what they’re doing, and it shows in every dish. If you’re around Lower Parel, make a stop here—you’ll thank me later. A word of praise for Indrajeet FnB executive who treated us like royalty.

The SoBo fried rice tasted good but was quite dry, and the portion size was underwhelming. The sushi didn’t work for me at all, lacked balance in flavors and texture. We were served rice crackers with five kinds of dips, which was a nice touch, though.

Some of my non-vegetarian friends tried the Thai-style chicken rice, and the feedback wasn’t great, dry and bland, unfortunately. For the six of us, the bill came up to ₹6,000, which felt steep considering the portion sizes.

The staff was polite and welcoming, though they seemed a bit short-handed. Service was decent but could’ve been quicker.

Overall, it’s a cute spot with potential, especially for the ambiance and those heavenly dimsums. But if you’re going for a full meal, don’t expect large portions or consistent quality across the menu.

featured_reviews.name: Prachiti Gadekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
During a recent visit to Yazu Pan Asian Supper Kitchen in Lower Parel, I had the opportunity to indulge in a diverse and flavorful spread that truly showcased the restaurant’s mastery over Asian cuisine. From the moment we arrived, the ambiance set the tone for a relaxed yet upscale dining experience. The service was courteous and efficient, with dishes arriving promptly and plated beautifully.

Our meal began with the Prawn Tempura Roll, which was light, crispy, and paired with just the right balance of sauces. It was followed by the Sriracha Chicken that packed a punch of heat, complemented by a slightly sweet undertone. The Yazu Signature Sichuan Garlic Prawn stood out with its bold flavors and perfectly cooked prawns, a definite must-try for seafood lovers. Another highlight was the Yazu Signature Chicken, which offered a rich and savory profile that paired well with the other mains.

For noodles, the Phad Thai Noodles were enjoyable, with a classic tamarind flavor and the right mix of textures. The Chicken in Hot Garlic Sauce added a spicy, garlicky depth to the meal that was satisfying and comforting. We also tried the Shojo, which added a refreshing and slightly lighter touch to the otherwise intense flavor profile of the dishes.

To end on a sweet note, we ordered the Mathilda Cakes Pull Me Up. It was a delightful dessert that offered a decadent and fun experience, perfectly capping off our evening.

Overall, Yazu delivered a memorable culinary experience with a well-rounded menu and elegant atmosphere. It's a great choice for those looking to explore Pan Asian cuisine with a modern twist in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavin Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazu is a Pan‑Asian “supper club” concept that brings together flavors from Japan, China, Thailand, Korea and Southeast Asia under one roof. The Lower Parel outlet is positioned as a flagship. The place is spacious combining indoor and outdoor elements. The branding emphasizes “visual experiences” — sculptural ceiling installations, patterned concrete flooring, carved wooden walls, lighting as focal décor elements. Ambience is amazing: stylish, atmospheric, good for evenings, date nights, or a premium outing. The décor and lighting get special and the ceiling installation, carved walls, and an aesthetic that’s “Instagram‑worthy.” After sundown, it transforms into a high‑energy bar/music venue  like “Studio Nights”.
Wide and ambitious menu: sushi, sashimi, maki, dim sum, baos (Taiwanese street bun), Teppanyaki, Robata grill items, curries, fusion dishes (e.g. “Asian Pizza‑San”) etc. They offer special dietary menus: Jain and Keto options. Go for signature dishes (e.g. sushi rolls, baos, dim sum) early; save room for dessert.
Top Picks:
• Black crispy Asparagus Roll (sushi) • Steamed Veg. Cheung Fung • Veg. Dimsum Experience Basket (7 piece) • Spicy Lotus root • Mah Poh Tofu etc.
• For soups: the Tom Kha, Tom Yum are superb.
• Desserts are also a highlight: “Pull Me Up Tiramisu”, “Berry Blossom Cheesecake”, “Salted Caramel Tart”, Coconut Panna Cotta etc. Presentation is premium, textures and flavors seem well balanced in many reviews.
• Drinks are highly inventive, globally inspired, and expertly crafted. Every sip is bold and gives unforgettable experience. Loved its Samurai (cocktail), Shojo and Yashi (mocktails) which were flavorful and refreshing.
Attentive and polite staff who guide through the menu, make recommendations, and ensure a comfortable dining experience. Yazu Lower Parel is a strong pick if you're looking for a premium Pan‑Asian dining + bar experience in Mumbai. The ambience, décor, and overall concept are standout features. The place has a premium, elegant vibe and delivers a memorable night out.

featured_reviews.name: Quresh Tyebji
featured_reviews.review_text:
YAZU delivers a standout lunch experience. The staff was warm, attentive, and genuinely courteous throughout, making the meal feel relaxed and welcoming.

The presentation was sublime—every dish was beautifully plated and thoughtfully executed. Highlights included the cream cheese truffle dumplings (the pink ones), hands down the best bite, and the mushroom money bags, crispy with great texture and depth of flavor. The YAZU signature chicken was bold and satisfying, and the wonton soup was light, comforting, and perfectly balanced.

The affogato and cold coffee were an excellent pairing too with the spicy flavors—smooth, rich, and a perfect way to wrap up lunch. A refined yet approachable Pan-Asian spot with fantastic food, strong attention to detail, and great service. Highly recommend.

featured_reviews.name: Anish Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:

From fresh sushi to flavourful dim sums, every dish is well-balanced and beautifully presented.
The vibe is chic and perfect for both chill outings and special evenings.
A place you’ll definitely keep coming back to for great food & vibes!

featured_reviews.name: jd
featured_reviews.review_text: Brunch goals! Last Sunday, my friend and I visited Yazu for brunch, and OMG it was SO GOOD! 🍴 They have tons of dishes on the menu, and I loved the range and variety in their sushi and dimsums. Their wok-tossed starters were amazing, especially the Sichuan peppercorn chicken 🤩. Yazu never fails to impress me with their top-notch Asian food 😍. I highly recommend everyone check out their brunch menu!

featured_reviews.name: Mishti Khadye
featured_reviews.review_text:
A place you will keep coming back to but do reserve your tables in adavance♥️
- Ambiance: They offer both indoor and outdoor seating, but I preferred the air-conditioned indoor area — it’s super cozy and perfect for a relaxed meal.
- Food: The food was outstanding! Made with high-quality ingredients, the dishes were light and didn’t feel heavy or weirdly rich.
Highlights:
- Cheung Fun (Prawn and Chicken): A personal fave! Loved the mix of flavors and textures.
- Sushi (Philadelphia and California): Amazing! Both were a spot on 🍣.
- Desserts: We went for the Chocolate Caramel Tart and Chocolate Soufflé. If you pick one, go for the Chocolate Soufflé — it’s _perfectly_ gooey and comes with ice cream. Both desserts had ice cream, but the soufflé stole my heart.
- Drinks: The drink menu has a variety of unique options; pick one (or two!) and dive in — you won’t go wrong.
- Service: The staff were humble, polite, and super attentive. They guided us through the menu, adjusted our table, fetched cutlery, phone stand, and even anticipated our needs without being asked. Big shoutout to Govind and the entire Yazu team — great job!
I’ll definitely be back!

featured_reviews.name: Divyaa Amburle
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazu Lower Parel: A Pan-Asian Gem!
Hey foodies! I just had an amazing night at Yazu in Lower Parel, Mumbai. This spot is all about bold Asian vibes with a modern twist. Let me break it down.
Ambiance: Super chic and cozy! Dim lights, sleek decor, and a warm buzz that makes you feel like you're in a fancy Tokyo hideout. Perfect for dates or chill hangs.

Food: Oh man, the flavors exploded! Tried the spicy ramen – rich, slurpy goodness. Dim sums were steamy and fresh, with crispy lobster rolls stealing the show. Even the veggie tofu rice bowl was spot-on tasty. Portions are generous, presentation on point. Total win!

Service: Staff is friendly and quick – they explained the menu like pros and kept drinks flowing. Attentive without hovering.

If you're craving Pan-Asian magic, rush to Yazu. It's worth every bite! Who's joining next?

featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited KOKO, Lower Parel, on a completely last-minute plan. Their lunch service goes on till 4:00 pm, with the last order taken at 3:15 pm. Luckily, we managed to reach just in time at 3:10 pm.

We ordered the KOKO Signature Roll (avocado, tempura asparagus, crisps, and KOKO sauce) along with Hong Kong Soy Noodles with chicken.

The sushi was the absolute highlight for me – crisp, fresh, and packed with layers of flavour. Every bite was a delight, and it’s definitely something I would love to come back for. The noodles, on the other hand, had a very balanced and subtle taste, making it a nice complement to the meal.

Overall, it was a great experience. The service was quick even though we ordered at the last moment, and the food quality was impressive. Good going, KOKO – I sincerely hope they continue maintaining these high standards!

featured_reviews.review_text: Where do i begin! Best meal i had in mumbai was at KOKO. The mushroom turnip cake, baby potatoes, signature sushi, the noodles , thai lemonade absolutely fire - 10/10. Service 11/10 and ambiance was great too! So worth it, definitely recommend this place if you’re in mumbai, hope they open in delhi soon :)

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Minal Kabra
featured_reviews.review_text:
KOKO, Lower Parel – A Luxe Asian Dining Experience

KOKO in Lower Parel offers a refined and memorable dining experience. The ambiance is top-notch — modern, elegant, and perfect for an evening out. The menu features an impressive variety of sushi and dim sum, with ample vegetarian choices that are just as flavorful and thoughtfully prepared as the non-vegetarian options.

The staff is courteous and attentive, adding to the overall premium feel of the place. However, a heads-up for first-timers — they don’t usually offer tables without a reservation, even if some appear to be vacant. Be prepared to sit at the bar if you walk in without prior booking.

That said, once you’re seated, the food and experience are absolutely worth it. For anyone who appreciates quality Asian cuisine in a sophisticated setting, KOKO is highly recommended — just make sure to reserve in advance!

featured_reviews.name: WK
featured_reviews.review_text:
THE PLACE TO BE!
Great location, super friendly staff and a great choice of high quality food for all diet restrictions. They even have special gluten free dishes. The first restaurant which even offers gluten-free soy sauce. Fantastic so even I could enjoy the wonderful flavour of soy sauce and miso soup.
You can ask the team for some extras like you want dishes without onions or garlic...
All the dishes were flavoured perfectly and with love.

The dessert was a creamy fluffy dream. And the espresso too.
Absolutely all on point.

Price wise it's not cheap. We paid 60 EUR ala cards. They have special brunches like the father's day brunch for 25 EUR plus taxes. These  prices are absolutely fair but eating ala cards is expensive as the portions are not that big.

Nevertheless a fantastic restaurant and we definitely will visit again as the food is incredibly good.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently dined at Asia Kitchen By Mainland China at the Palladium Mall. While the presentation of the dishes was excellent and visually appealing, the overall culinary experience was strictly average.
Here is a breakdown of what we ordered:
* **Raw Papaya Salad (Som Tum):** Served in a very unique, jagged-edged dark bowl, the salad had a good crunch from the fresh papaya, carrots, and peanuts. However, the dressing felt muted and lacked the sharp, spicy-sour punch that usually makes this dish stand out.
* **Vegetarian Sushi Rolls:** We tried two varieties. One featured asparagus and a generous topping of tempura crunch with spicy mayo, while the other was garnished with spicy mayo and black sesame seeds. Both were beautifully presented on marble slabs over bamboo leaves with fresh ginger and wasabi. The textures were decent, but the flavors were quite standard.
* **Yellow Vegetable Curry:** This was a rich, creamy, and comforting curry loaded with vegetables like broccoli and carrots. It was served nicely in a white bowl resting on a large, textured rustic plate. It was probably the most satisfying dish of the meal, though not highly unique.
* **Vegetable Fried Rice with Dark Gravy:** A hearty portion of fried rice served alongside a dark, soy-based vegetable stir-fry. It was functional and filling, but the seasoning of the gravy was a bit one-dimensional.
* **Noodles with Red Veg Stir-fry:** Thin yellow noodles paired with a reddish, saucy vegetable mix. Similar to the rice, it was decent but lacked a signature flavor to make it memorable.
* **Beverages:** We had a couple of iced drinks, including a refreshing orange-garnished mocktail/cocktail and a lime drink. They were cool and refreshing accompaniments to the meal.
**Overall Verdict:**
The aesthetic and plating at this restaurant are commendable, and it’s a fine, filling option if you are already shopping at the mall and want a vegetarian-friendly Asian spread. However, for a specialty Pan-Asian restaurant, the flavors played it too safe. It was an average experience that looked a bit better than it tasted."

Dining at By The Mekong, located at the Penthouse level of The St. Regis Mumbai, was an exceptional experience.
We began with the Prosperity Salad created for the Chinese New Year of the Horse, a vibrant mix of freshly grated vegetables, salmon, sesame seeds and their signature hoisin sauce. As a salad lover, this was a clear highlight, beautifully balanced in flavour and texture.
The appetizers reflected impressive freshness and finesse, from the radish cake and steamed prawns with lotus root in chili oyster sauce to the lotus root and water chestnut preparation and the delicately balanced sweet and sour tofu.
The zodiac inspired cocktail presentation added a thoughtful touch. I tried the Carthern, a gin based cocktail with subtle kiwi notes, while the Bombay Masala and cranberry mocktails were refreshing and layered.
For the main course, the burnt garlic fried rice, Hakka noodles and white garlic gravy with exotic vegetables were comforting and well executed. The Mongolian lamb chops stood out for their refined presentation and beautifully executed flavours.
Dessert was indulgent yet balanced. The Cacao 64, with rich cacao, chocolate soil, raspberry sorbet and a touch of rock salt, was perfect for a chocolate lover. The ice cream coupe with custard apple, chocolate and vanilla was equally delightful. On my next visit, I look forward to trying the Air Brulee and the Umpiw chicken.
The menu curated by Master Chef Li Qiang reflects over two decades of experience, with dishes that are bold, elegant and subtly layered. Paired with stunning views of the Mumbai skyline from the 37th floor and contemporary chandelier style lighting, the ambience elevates the entire experience.
A special mention to Assistant Manager Newlai for her warm hospitality and for helping capture some wonderful pictures. For those who love documenting their dining experiences, she truly does a great job.

This was one of the most bizarre “luxury dining” experiences I’ve had in a long time.

It became even stranger when I asked for the bill. Instead of simply bringing it and allowing me to leave, staff repeatedly pushed dessert and continued trying to upsell even while I was holding my card ready to pay. The inability to read basic social cues was honestly astonishing.

The final touch was staff loudly shouting my name across the restaurant and then after me as I was leaving. In a property positioning itself as luxury hospitality, discretion should be the absolute minimum standard.

Good service is not constant interruption, aggressive upselling, performative attentiveness or hovering over guests. Good service is calm, intuitive, discreet and respectful of personal space.

The food itself was perfectly fine, which almost makes the service stand out even more negatively. I have genuinely experienced more relaxed and emotionally intelligent hospitality in far less expensive places.

featured_reviews.name: R Irani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Situated in Kamla mills compound, this outlet of Wok Express serving a range of Asian food resonates with shades of black and brown with its use of granite and wood in the furnishings. Simple yet warm! The place can accommodate upto twenty five people in one time however the low stools and tables in the centre are not as spaced out as the high stools on the side and it thus becomes a bit difficult to move around.

Coming to the food, we began with the Chilli Paneer Bao which was in our opinion the best dish of all that we reviewed. Sweet steamed Chinese buns that are "as soft as the cloud" filled with truly "melt in the mouth" cottage cheese cubes tossed with whole green chillies that lends the spice to the sweet bao. Recommended!

Among the Japanese stuff, we tried the newly introduced Veg Schezwan Sushi that had seven sweet and sour rice rolls filled with mix veggies like carrots and green bell peppers, topped with spicy schezwan chutney. Served with wasabi and pickled ginger strips, this one is a burst of flavours!

From the appetizers we had the Kung Pao Potato and the newly introduced Pepper Garlic Paneer. While the former had unpeeled baby potatoes tossed in sweet Kung Pao sauce along with cashews to add some crunch, as well as spring onions and dry red chillies, we would suggest having the Pepper Garlic Paneer that had a smoky flavour with chewy cottage cheese cubes sauteed along with mix bell peppers and onions.

In the main course we tried the Exotic Veggies in Chilli Soya Sauce with Burnt Garlic Rice. The sauce came with a whole lot of mushrooms, broccoli, zucchini, yellow bell peppers and pak choy that went well with the otherwise dull garlic rice as it had no burnt flavour. We gave our feedback for the same and they have promised to work on this one.

The Wok can either be personalised or you can choose from the pre-set Chef recommended options available in case you can't decide or have no time to wrack your head for the same. I made my own personal wok with a base of Flat Wheat Noodles since the healthier Wheat Soba noodles weren't available then. Veggies including carrots, french beans, broccoli and tofu as protein were tossed in with the red chilli pepper sauce, topped with condiments like fried onion, crushed peanuts and fresh cilantro to complete my Wok. It's a meal in itself and the best option for a quick on-the-go lunch!

The quantity for this, as well as the other things we had is very good and the ingredients are fresh. They are honest if something isn't available and that's what good brands are about.

My only disappointment apart from the garlic rice was the desserts. I have been associated with Wok Express since it first opened in Bandra and for more than two years now they still have no eggless dessert options. I would really appreciate if they could introduce a veg version of their popular Fortune Cookie. We had to end half-heartedly with the Very Berry Strawberry ice cream from Baskin and Robins

featured_reviews.name: Atul Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Chinese Xpress is easy to locate, though it offers 2 small and functional spaces with enough seating. The interior is basic and bland, certainly not designed for a special occasion. This spot is best suited for a quick, casual meal with friends, or as a reliable option for takeaway or online ordering. A quick note for seafood lovers: prawns were unavailable during my visit.

The Culinary Experience
The menu offers solid Indo-Chinese options with generally decent portion sizes that are good for sharing between two people.

Teriyaki Chicken Dry (starter): This was the clear winner of the meal, an easy 4 out of 5. The chicken was exceptionally soft and the Teriyaki flavour was spot on, making it a very enjoyable starter.

Chicken Hot Basil Dry (starter): This dish was also good, scoring a 3.5 out of 5. While the flavour was delicious, the texture was slightly tighter or chewier. However, this is likely inherent to the style of preparation, so the rating is a personal preference rather than a fault in the cooking.

For the main course, I tried the Chicken Chopper Fried Rice. The rice itself was satisfactory (3 out of 5), but it was topped with a gravy that, unfortunately, was the weakest link of the meal (2 out of 5). Thankfully, the portion of the topping was minimal and easily separable, allowing the fried rice to be enjoyed mostly on its own.

Overall Verdict
Chinese Xpress is a straightforward, no-frills destination offering good value and tasty starters, particularly the Teriyaki Chicken. It's a highly recommended spot for a casual, budget-friendly meal with a group or, even better, for a satisfying, quick takeaway at home.
